---
title: "VSTOL"
subtitle: "Variant Standardization, Tabulation, and Operations Library"
---

VSTOL standardizes small and structural DNA variants from VCF files into the
[Occam's Variant Grammar](https://pirlblog.substack.com/p/variant-standardization)
TSV format, then runs list operations — annotate, diff, intersect, merge,
collapse, and overlap — on the standardized variant lists.

## Quick Start

### 1. Install

`vstol` is available on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/vstol/):

```bash
pip install vstol
```

### 2. See What's Available

```bash
vstol --help
```

Or browse the [Commands](cli/index.qmd) reference for every subcommand and its
options.

### 3. Standardize, then operate

Convert each caller's VCF to the Occam's Variant Grammar TSV with
[`vcf2tsv`](cli/vcf2tsv.qmd), then compose the set operations over the resulting
lists.

## How VSTOL is Organized

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-6}
### Standardization
[`vcf2tsv`](cli/vcf2tsv.qmd) converts a variant caller's VCF into the Occam's
Variant Grammar TSV — the common format every other command consumes.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
### Set operations
[`diff`](cli/diff.qmd), [`intersect`](cli/intersect.qmd),
[`merge`](cli/merge.qmd), and [`collapse`](cli/collapse.qmd) compare and combine
variant lists across samples, callers, or runs.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
### Annotation
[`annotate`](cli/annotate.qmd) adds gene-level context (e.g. GENCODE) to a
standardized variant list.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
### Region overlap
[`overlap`](cli/overlap.qmd) selects variants whose breakpoints fall within (or
near) a list of genomic regions.
:::

:::

## Dependencies

* python (>=3.10)
* pandas (>=2.0.3)
* numpy (>=1.22.3)
* networkx (>=3.4.2)
* intervaltree (>=3.1.0)
